newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria says autumn sowing on schedule.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria says autumn sowing on schedule.

text.p: Bulgaria should not face bread shortages next year as enough wheat for human consumption has been sown, Agriculture Minister Krastyo Trendafilov said on Friday.
"If the weather conditions are favourable, the country's bread for 1997 has been secured," Trendafilov told parliament.
He said 1.4 million hectares of wheat and barley had been sown so far this autumn of the planned 1.6 million ha.
Last year the country planted one million ha of wheat and and 270,000 ha of barley.
Parliament passed a law in October unblocking farmers' funds from banks placed in receivership by the central bank.
Under the bill, the purchase prices of wheat, maize and barley from the 1996/97 harvest will be no less than 80 percent of the international price.
Those measures, plus good weather which prolonged the planting period, boosted plantings.
Low domestic prices encouraged high exports last year which combined with a poor harvest last summer to produce an acute grain shortage.
